file.content: Todos

lines: li input[type="checkbox"] { width: 1.1rem; height: 1.1rem; margin: 0; cursor: pointer; }
+  /* [REQ-004] Priority colour: left stripe, set after overdue so it keeps its own colour. */
.filters button { background: transparent; color: #1c1917; border: 1px solid #d6d3d1; padding: 0.35rem 0.75rem; }
<input type="text" data-testid="todo-input" placeholder="What needs doing?" autocomplete="off" aria-label="New todo">
+  // [REQ-004] Only low, med or high; anything else (including older todos) is med.
// [REQ-003] due is optional, stored as a YYYY-MM-DD string or ''.
-    todos.push({ id: makeId(), text: text, createdAt: Date.now(), completed: false, due: normalizeDue(due) });
+    todos.push({ id: makeId(), text: text, createdAt: Date.now(), completed: false, due: normalizeDue(due), priority: normalizePriority(priority) }); // [REQ-004]

content.text:
I added priorities: a `todo-priority` select (Low/Med/High, Med by default and reset to Med after each add), `data-priority` on every `todo-item`, and a coloured left stripe on each row (high red, med amber, low grey). I haven't opened it in a browser.
Older todos with no saved priority show as `med`. The stripe is separate from the red overdue styling, so both show at once, and completed todos still sit below active ones.
I didn't tint the whole row by priority, because that would clash with the red overdue background.
